adds.title: Sharia Implementation in Northern Nigeria 1999-2006: A Sourcebook, Vol. III, Ch. 3 Part IV — Documentary Materials (Ostien, ed.)
adds.summary: Ostien's Volume III reproduces Borno State's own statute on prostitution, homosexuality, brothels and other sexual immoralities (2000), gazetted in Borno State Gazette No. 42 Vol. 26 on 18 October 2001 and signed by Governor Kachalla on 10 December 2000. Section 3 makes engaging in prostitution, lesbianism, a homosexual act or pimping an offence in the State; Section 7 provides that any person who 'engages in sexual intercourse with another person of the same gender shall upon conviction be punished with death'; Section 4 deems all brothels closed on commencement; and Section 9 assigns jurisdiction to the Upper Sharia Courts, Area Courts and Magistrate Courts. Borno's own enacted death penalty for same-gender intercourse independently supports this record's finding that the state's legal architecture, not just the national framework, criminalises same-sex conduct.

adds.title: Sharia Implementation in Northern Nigeria 1999-2006: A Sourcebook, Vol. IV, Ch. 4 Part III — The Sharia Penal Codes (Ostien, ed.)
adds.summary: The sourcebook's list of enacted Sharia Penal Codes records Borno's Sharia Penal Code Law 2001, signed into law on 3 March 2003, with no operation date or gazette identified; the editor notes the Borno text was obtained only in May 2006, after the volume's annotation had been completed, which is why Borno is not among the individually annotated codes. Confirms Borno enacted its own state Sharia Penal Code legislation in addition to its secular morality law, so the record's claimed parallel Sharia layer for Borno rests on a Borno-specific enactment rather than mere umbrella coverage.

adds.title: Nigerian Security Operatives Arrest 76 Suspects At Same-Sex Wedding In Gombe State
adds.summary: In October 2023 the Gombe State Command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) raided a homosexual birthday gathering at Duwa Plaza along the Bauchi-Gombe Expressway that was preparing a same-sex wedding, arresting 76 people; state PRO Buhari Sa'ad told reporters that 59 males were detained with 21 wilfully confessing to being homosexuals, along with 17 females present at the scene, and that they 'will be charged to court to answer for their crime which is on social vice; a crime in Gombe State.' The first incident-level evidence in this dossier that Gombe enforces its moral-crimes layer on the ground, with local charging of attendees.

adds.title: Civil Defence arrests 76 people at same-sex birthday, planned wedding in Gombe | The Guardian Nigeria News
adds.summary: The Lagos daily The Guardian, byline James Agberebi, published 23 October 2023, reports that about 76 people were arrested after a tip-off about a same-sex birthday party and planned marriage in Gombe State; Gombe NSCDC Commandant Mohammed Muazu confirmed the arrests, spokesperson Buhari Saad said 21 of the 59 detained males were involved in gay activities while the remaining males and the 17 females were invited guests and onlookers, and officers voiced concern over the participants' ages. Independent Lagos-press confirmation of the same October 2023 Gombe mass arrest, archived from the live Guardian Nigeria URL on 4 December 2023.

adds.title: Sharia Implementation in Northern Nigeria 1999-2006: A Sourcebook, Vol. IV, Ch. 4 Part III — The Sharia Penal Codes (Ostien, ed.)
adds.summary: The annotated volume records Gombe's Sharia Penal Code Law 2001, signed into law on 23 November 2001, and annotates its text: Gombe, Jigawa, Kano and Zamfara share the sodomy offence punishing unmarried men with caning of 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death (rajm); the lesbianism offence carries up to 50 lashes plus imprisonment of up to six months; and Gombe defines gross indecency in its own formulation as 'any sexual offence against the normal or usual standards of behaviour.' The state's enacted statutory text behind this record's claim that Gombe's Sharia layer criminalises same-sex conduct by men and women beyond the federal code.

adds.title: Nigeria: Sexual orientation and gender identity or expression — Country Policy and Information Note (UK Home Office, June 2025)
adds.summary: The UK Home Office's June 2025 country note carries a twelve-state Sharia penalties table with Jigawa's own row: Sharia Penal Code (2000) — 'Married men: death by stoning,' 'Unmarried men: 100 lashes and imprisonment for up to one year,' and up to 50 lashes with imprisonment for up to 6 months for same-sex acts between women; section 8.2.20 points to the note's Sharia section on the codes in force in Kano, Borno, Kaduna and other northern states. Dated government confirmation that Jigawa's Sharia penal layer remains the operative criminal frame for Muslims in the state, matching this record's June 2025 country-of-origin note claim.

adds.title: Sharia Implementation in Northern Nigeria 1999-2006: A Sourcebook, Vol. IV, Ch. 4 Part III — The Sharia Penal Codes (Ostien, ed.)
adds.summary: The sourcebook lists Jigawa's Sharia Penal Code Law 2000, Law No. 12 of 2000, signed into law on 18 December 2000 and coming into operation on 27 December 2000 (Jigawa State Gazette Vol. 1 No. 12), and annotates Jigawa among the four states (with Gombe, Kano and Zamfara) whose sodomy offence punishes unmarried men with 100 lashes plus one year's imprisonment and married men with stoning to death (rajm); lesbianism carries up to 50 lashes plus up to six months' imprisonment, with Jigawa including the 'unnatural fusion of the female sexual organs' explanation of the offence. Enactment-level detail for the record's claim that Jigawa's 1999-2002-wave code criminalises acts the federal code does not reach, including women's same-sex conduct.

adds.title: LGBT rights in Mexico (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Mexico-wide LGBT rights article carries San Luis Potosí-specific facts: on 17 May 2019 the state began authorizing legal gender changes for transgender people, and on 21 May 2019 same-sex marriage took effect after the state Congress voted 14-12 in favour on 16 May 2019, with joint adoption by same-sex couples legal in the state from the same month. The article lists San Luis Potosí among the states that enacted a gender-identity law in 2019 and among those whose hate-crime statutes recognize motivation by gender and sexual preference, while noting its local law bans discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender but not gender identity. This confirms the record's claim of a 2019 civil-registry reform creating an administrative gender-recognition procedure and adds the marriage and adoption dates a trans visitor would rely on.

adds.title: LGBT rights in Mexico (Wikipedia)
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Mexico-wide LGBT rights article reports Sinaloa-specific events: the Mexican Supreme Court ordered the state to legalize same-sex marriage within 90 days on 15 May 2018, and the Sinaloa Congress passed a same-sex marriage law on 15 June 2021, with civil unions for both same-sex and opposite-sex couples performed in the state. The same article lists Sinaloa among states whose local law bans discrimination on grounds of both sexual orientation and gender identity, among those with hate-crime statutes covering gender and sexual preference, and among the states that enacted a gender-identity recognition law, dated 2022 there. That 2022 dating conflicts with the March 2025 HRW count cited in the record's existing sources that Sinaloa had legislated no legal gender-recognition procedure, so the state's actual local-law status needs verification against the state code before relying on either account.
